title: What If You Fell Into Saturn?

scenes.text: What if you fell into Saturn? There's no ground to hit, and that's the problem.
Saturn has no solid surface. The gas just gets thicker and hotter the deeper you go.
At the equator, winds blow east at about a thousand miles an hour.
At the level where pressure matches Earth's sea level, it's about minus 217 degrees Fahrenheit.
Go deeper and temperatures climb into the thousands of degrees, with pressure past one million times Earth's.
There's never a floor. The gas slowly turns into hot liquid hydrogen, with no sharp line between the two.
